Subject: Post-call: retention windows, backups, and SOC 2 status (Helix)

Hi Jenna — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and our proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- SOC 2: you mentioned a recent SOC 2 Type II report in 2026 and that a refreshed attestation is due Q4 2027. Can you confirm whether the report covers the Redwood-hosted environment or only your internal services?
- Retention & deletion: Helix wants a deletion SLA for customer data and a separate log retention policy. On the call you said the clinical product requires 13 months for patient records (HIPAA), and audit/logs retention could be longer. We need explicit RPO/RTO expectations for backups and the maximum retention window for logs/backups to surface in contract language.
- Backups: Please confirm whether backups are encrypted with customer-managed keys or Helix-managed keys and whether you require immutable backups/retention hold support.
- Vendor security questionnaire: you said you'd share the questionnaire; once we have it we can map controls and surface any gaps.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Jenna: send questionnaire + link to current SOC 2 report (or redacted attestation).
2) Redwood (me + Karthik): provide a short (1–2 page) retention & backup summary for Helix and call out deletion SLA, RPO/RTO ranges, and restore testing cadence.
3) If any gaps, schedule a 20-min follow-up to finalize language for the PO/contract.

I've attached a short template we use for retention windows (attachment: redwood-retention-template.xlsx) to accelerate mapping. If you prefer, we can also do the follow-up call later today.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Torres <j.torres@helixhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: retention windows, backups, and SOC 2 status (Helix)

Hi Jenna — appreciate the quick turnaround. Ben, Karthik and I put together a short retention/backup summary tailored for Helix; attaching redwood-retention-summary-helix.pdf. The doc highlights:

- Default retention windows: conversational/temporary data = 30 days; embeddings/processed artifacts = configurable (30–540 days depending on contract).
- Deletion SLA: standard is 30 days from request for application-layer deletion, with cryptographic erasure of derived caches within 72 hours; contractable to 7/14/30/90-day windows depending on workload and compliance class.
- Backups: incremental block backups (encrypted at rest), standard RPO ~4 hrs, RTO for typical restores ~6–24 hrs depending on dataset size; point-in-time restores available for dedicated deployments.
- Keys: we support Helix-managed CMKs for Private deployments and HSM-backed keys for enterprise Private installs; hosted accounts can request CMK integration with approval.

Can we book a short 20-min call tomorrow to confirm which datasets need 13 vs 18 months and whether immutable backups are required for any subset? If the Helix team prefers, we can also draft contract language for the deletion SLA and RPO/RTO ranges now.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-retention-summary-helix.pdf (PDF stub)
